headline: Intel's 29% crash and Amazon's cash burn sink chips; SOX −7.2%, S&P 500 worst day since June
summary: A tech-led rout rather than a broad collapse. Stocks opened lower after the Amazon and Intel reports and slid to session lows in the afternoon, when the VIX touched 22.31, before trimming losses into the close; tech lost about 4.9% and chips 7.2%, yet six of 11 sectors rose and nearly as many S&P 500 members gained as fell, led by energy and consumer staples.
drivers: Intel sank 28.6% to $65.76 after guiding Q4 sales roughly 9% below estimates, blaming weaker PC demand as memory-driven price increases put off buyers. The SOX fell 7.2% with 29 of its 30 members lower, leaving it down more than 15% for October.

AMD dropped 10.9%, SanDisk 13.5%, TSMC 6.0%, Broadcom 5.5%, Micron 5.3% and Nvidia 4.2%, which slipped behind Apple in market value; server makers Dell (−10.8%) and HP (−9.6%) also slid. The Nasdaq is now 7.8% below its Oct 6 record after Alphabet's plunge the day before.
Amazon misses and keeps burning cash

Amazon missed on revenue ($201.9 billion) and EPS ($1.89), and its trailing free cash flow swung to an outflow of more than $42 billion on AI-related capex. The stock was down about 7% before the open but pared that to −1.4% as AWS grew 39%.

Treasuries rallied, taking the 10-year down about 4bp to 4.94% and the 2-year about 5bp to 4.56%, while energy (+1.9%) and staples (+1.4%) gained as Exxon (+2.2%), Chevron (+1.8%) and Mondelez (+3.9%) beat forecasts. WTI rose 2.1% to a six-month high of $104.12 after tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz.
week: For the week the S&P 500 fell 0.6%, the Dow 0.9% and the Nasdaq 2.0% while the Russell 2000 rose 1.3%; the backdrop is a Fed on hold at 3.75–4% with a December hike largely priced, a 10-year yield back under 5% after topping 5.30% early in the month, and oil up about 15% in October.
watch: Next: Apple and Palantir report Monday after the close, AMD on Tuesday evening alongside the Nov 3 midterms, Arm and Qualcomm on Wednesday, and the October jobs report on Friday, Nov 6.
